how: Kept by hand. Clubs, sessions and races were read on 23 Nov 2026 from the organisers' own registration pages (runsignup.com), Go To Bermuda event listings, Bernews, The Royal Gazette and the World Triathlon site, the clubs' own websites, the PGA TOUR site and amateurgolf.com. Only what those pages say is here. Most 2027 calendars were not yet published, so past races are listed as the usual calendar with their 2025 or 2026 dates. Add each new season when it is announced and move review_after on. An event with an 'end' date drops into the usual calendar once that date has passed.

sports.name: Running
sports.lead: Clubs, the weekly group run, and the big race weekend in January.

bodies.name: Bermuda National Athletics Association
bodies.what: The national body. Listed as organiser of the Chubb Bermuda Triangle Challenge.

bodies.name: Mid Atlantic Athletic Club
bodies.what: The island's road running club. It puts on its own races, such as the No Frills 5K and 10K at Clearwater Beach each September, and members get 10% off Triangle Challenge entries.

bodies.name: Grateful Miles Run Club
bodies.what: A community run club for all levels, with a group run every Sunday.

sessions.note: All levels. Listed weekly until 21 March 2027.

events.name: Chubb Bermuda Triangle Challenge
events.where: Hamilton, the National Sports Centre and Dockyard
note: Three races in three days. Friday 7pm: the Butterfield Mile on Front Street. Saturday 9am: the Allshores 10K at the National Sports Centre, with a 5K run at 9:05 and a 5K walk at 9:10. Sunday 7am: the PwC Bermuda Marathon and Half Marathon.
2027 is the 50th running of the marathon.
The full challenge is the mile, the 10K and the marathon. The half challenge swaps in the half marathon.
Pasta dinner on Saturday 16 January, 6 to 8pm at the Hamilton Princess, $50, with Dame Flora Duffy as guest speaker.

events.name: Rum to the Beach
note: A 7.13 mile race that many use as a warm up for the Triangle Challenge.

events.name: MAAC No Frills 5K and 10K
events.where: Clearwater Beach car park, St David's
note: Run by the Mid Atlantic Athletic Club.

sports.name: Cycling
sports.lead: The association, how race mornings work, and the races that come round each year.

bodies.name: Bermuda Bicycle Association
bodies.what: Founded in 1974. It runs the road and mountain bike race calendar, promotes Cycling for All club rides, develops junior riders and sends teams overseas. You must be a member to race: join through racedayworld.com.

sessions.note: The association promotes open club rides, but I found no published times. Check its website or Facebook page.

tips: A typical race morning starts with the juniors at about 8am, then the C category and women for 25 to 30 minutes, then the A and B categories for 35 to 40 minutes. Racing is usually over by 9:30 or 10am.
Adults usually pay $20 to $30 a race. Juniors often race free.

events.name: President's Cup road race
events.where: From No. 1 Car Park, Front Street, Hamilton, 7:30am
note: About 54 miles. $30 for adults and $15 for juniors, for riders of racing age 15 and up.

events.name: Criterium races
events.where: Lamb Foggo and the Fort Knox loop in St David's, and Cross Island at Dockyard
note: Short circuit races, including the National Criterium Championships.

events.name: Individual and team time trials
events.where: Kindley Field Road, St David's, among others
note: Riders set off one at a time against the clock. Start times are sent out by email the day before.

sports.name: Triathlon
sports.lead: The association, what you need to enter, and the races of the year.

bodies.name: Bermuda Triathlon Association
bodies.what: Runs the race calendar. Every competitor must be a member, and race entries include a $10 one day membership for those who are not. Join through racedayworld.com. Every race needs volunteers.

tips: Races are not draft legal: no riding in another rider's slipstream.
Juniors may use a mountain bike or a road bike.
No headphones while racing. Whether wetsuits are allowed depends on the water and air temperature on the day.

events.name: Cambridge Beaches Bermuda Triathlon
note: Swim, bike and run from the resort.

events.name: Americas Triathlon CARIFTA Championships
note: The regional junior championships, hosted in Bermuda in 2026. Sprint distance for the 17 to 21 age group: 750 metre swim, 20 km bike, 5 km run.

events.name: Olympic distance triathlon
note: With a team option.

events.name: National Sprint Triathlon Championships
note: Adult individual and team races, plus junior races.

events.name: Mixed Team Relay National Championship
note: Short legs, with junior divisions from age 7.

sports.name: Sailing
sports.lead: The clubs, the weekly racing, and the regattas worth watching from shore.

bodies.name: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
bodies.what: 15 Point Pleasant Road, Hamilton. Founded in 1844. Co-organiser of the Newport Bermuda Race and manager of the Antigua Bermuda Race, and a Royal Yachting Association training centre with learn to sail courses. It is free to walk down and look at the boats when a fleet is in.

bodies.name: Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club
bodies.what: Pomander Road, Paget. Founded in 1882 and the only dinghy club in the world with a royal title. Home to Bermuda's largest junior sailing fleet, with sailing lessons for juniors and adults all year, and the host of Wednesday Night Racing.

bodies.name: St George's Dinghy and Sports Club
bodies.what: On the waterfront of St George's Harbour. Home of the fitted dinghy Victory IV, and host of the opening day of the fitted dinghy season.

bodies.name: Sandys Boat Club
bodies.what: Mangrove Bay, Somerset. Home of the fitted dinghy Challenger II, christened in 1990.

bodies.name: West End Sailboat Club
bodies.what: Somerset. Founded in 1941 by a group of Somerset sailors and boat builders, and the home of the Edward Cross Long Distance Comet Race.

bodies.name: Mid Atlantic Boat and Sports Club
bodies.what: Founded in 1944. One of the three clubs that race Comets.

bodies.name: East End Mini Yacht Club
bodies.what: Convict Bay, St George's. Racing Comets since 1968, from the same building it started in.

bodies.name: Endeavour Community Sailing
bodies.what: The youth programme that grew out of the America's Cup. It teaches schoolchildren to sail from bases at each end of the island.

events.name: Bermuda fitted dinghy season
events.when: Late May to early September (the 2026 season opened on Sunday 24 May)
events.where: St George's Harbour, Hamilton Harbour, Granaway Deep and Mangrove Bay
note: Four boats race for their clubs: Contest III for the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club, Elizabeth II for the Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club, Victory IV for St George's and Challenger II for Sandys.
Opening day in 2026 had three races, at noon, 1:30pm and 3pm, in St George's Harbour.

events.name: Edward Cross Long Distance Comet Race
events.when: National Heroes Day weekend in June
note: Comets from the West End Sailboat Club, the Mid Atlantic Boat and Sports Club and the East End Mini Yacht Club race the length of the island for the Edward Cross Memorial Cup.

events.name: SailGP
note: The international foiling catamaran league is due back on the Great Sound in 2027.

events.name: Newport Bermuda Race
events.when: June, every second year (started 19 June in 2026)
note: 635 miles from Newport, Rhode Island, and one of the oldest ocean races in the world, first sailed in 1906. Run by the Cruising Club of America and the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club. The next one is due in 2028.

events.name: Antigua Bermuda Race
events.when: Late April into May (started 29 April in 2026)
note: About 935 nautical miles from Antigua, managed by the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club.

events.name: Bermuda International Invitational Race Week
note: A week of keelboat racing hosted by the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club.

events.name: Bermuda Gold Cup
note: Match racing in Hamilton Harbour.

sessions.where: Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club, Paget
sessions.note: The club's most popular series, open to boats from every local club. Ask the club's sailing office about crewing.

tips: A fitted dinghy is only 14 feet long but carries a huge spread of sail and a crew of six. Crews have been known to jump overboard mid race to lighten the boat.
Good places to watch fitted dinghy racing: the wharves on the St George's waterfront, and Mangrove Bay in Somerset.
Comet racing grew up in Bermuda's historically Black boat clubs in the 1940s, and the long distance race has been sailed since 1944.

sports.name: Power boats
sports.lead: The racing season, where to watch, and the Round the Island race.

bodies.name: Bermuda Power Boat Association
bodies.what: Runs the national championship season from May to September. Racing is free to watch from shore.

tips: Race days at Ferry Reach run between 10am and 5pm, and the water is closed to other boats and patrolled.
Round the Island is often postponed for weather. In 2025 it moved twice because of small craft warnings, so check on the morning.

events.name: Rubis Round the Island
events.when: August (9 August in 2026, with 16 and 23 August as backup dates)
note: The big one: the fleet races right round Bermuda. Free to watch from anywhere on the coast.

events.name: Ferry Reach races
events.when: May to September (the 2026 season opened here on 3 May and returned on 13 September)
note: Closed circuit racing close to shore.

events.name: Hamilton Harbour race
note: Closed circuit racing in front of the city.

events.name: St George's and Cross Island races
events.when: Through the season (St George's was 30 August in 2026)
note: The season also visits Cross Island at Dockyard and ended in 2026 with a race at Spanish Point Boat Club on 27 September.

sports.source_note: 2026 schedule from Bernews, 9 May 2026. The 2027 schedule was not out when this was written.

sports.name: Golf
sports.lead: Seven courses on 21 square miles: where you can play, what it costs, and the tournaments.

places.name: Port Royal Golf Course
places.what: The Government's championship course, designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr. and opened in 1970, and home of the PGA TOUR event each autumn. The 16th plays 235 yards along the cliff edge. Visitors pay about $200 a round, with a cart extra. It shares playing privileges with Ocean View.

places.name: Ocean View Golf Course
places.what: The affordable one, on the North Shore. Listed at $60 for 18 holes, $40 for nine, and $40 at sunset. Lessons from $60 for half an hour.

places.name: Belmont Hills Golf Club
places.what: A hilly course with tiered greens and views over Hamilton Harbour, redesigned by Algie M. Pulley Jr. Listed at $110 for 18 holes.

places.name: Turtle Hill Golf Club
places.what: The par 3 course on the hill at the Fairmont Southampton, designed by Theodore Robinson. It offers night golf and FootGolf.

places.name: Five Forts Golf Club
places.kind: St George's. 18 holes, par 62. Resort, open to the public.
places.what: A short Robert Trent Jones Sr. course at the St. Regis, ringed by five old forts and looking out to sea.

places.name: Tucker's Point Golf Club
places.what: Beside the Rosewood. Laid out by Charles Banks and redesigned by Roger Rulewich.

places.name: The Mid Ocean Club
places.what: The Charles Blair Macdonald classic. Members only, but guests can book on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

bodies.name: Bermuda Golf Association
bodies.what: The national body. It runs the national championships, which are open to its members and to visitors with a current handicap.

tips: Fees change with the season and the time of day, and some sources disagree, so treat the prices here as a guide and check with the course.
There is also an 18 hole mini golf course, Bermuda Fun Golf, at Dockyard.

events.name: Butterfield Bermuda Championship
note: Bermuda's PGA TOUR event, first played in 2019. It moved to October in 2026 from mid November the year before. Spectator tickets started at about $38.

events.name: Goslings Bermuda Open
note: The national open, 54 holes for professionals and low handicap amateurs. The winner earns a place in the Butterfield Bermuda Championship.

events.name: Bermuda Stroke Play Championship
note: The 54 hole national stroke play title.

events.name: Bermuda Match Play Championship
note: A stroke play qualifying round on the Friday, then match play on Saturday and Sunday, with men's and senior divisions.

events.name: Bermuda Ladies Pro-Am Golf Classic
events.when: March (8 to 14 March in 2026, the 27th year)
note: Up to 20 teams, each of one woman professional and three amateurs.

sports.source_note: Course details from Go To Bermuda. 2027 tournament dates were not out when this was written.
